_what: VOICE MAPPING — PACK DATA. Which voice speaks which dialect, per learner FORM. §4 of the edu skill names voice mapping as pack, not engine — this is that file.
_rule: A LANGUAGE NAME IS NOT A VOICE. A multilingual voice that can pronounce Thai is still an English speaker pronouncing Thai: the learner copies the accent, and unlearns it at cost. Every dialect here names a NATIVE voice, and an entry with no native voice says so out loud instead of borrowing one.
_verified: 2026-10-17 — /v1/voices on the fleet account held 34 voices and not one was Thai (every label 'en', one 'es', one 'ru'). th-TH was wired to CwhRBWXzGAHq8TQ4Fs17 'Roger' (accent=american). Two Thai voices were then ADDED from the shared library (free — adds do not consume characters) and are verified present.
_add_a_voice: Shared voices are NOT synthesis-capable by id alone — POST /v1/voices/add/{public_owner_id}/{voice_id} first, or /text-to-speech returns 404 voice_not_found. That missing step is what 'the voice 404s' means.

th-TH.note: Preecha (th, male — 'Patient, Friendly, Clear') for Jordan; Kanya (th, female — 'Warm, Calm Narrator') for Josephine. A learner copies the voice they hear, so the voice must match the learner's own particle.

bridge._what: THE BRIDGE — the Latin reading (`rom`) said ALOUD, so the learner hears the approximation beside the real Thai. A bridge is only a bridge if it is spoken in the learner's OWN first language. Jordan, 2026-10-17: 'I am American, so I speak English… Josephine, she's Filipino, so she speaks Tagalog… speak to her and her language whenever she is asking for pronunciation.' An English-eye reading does not serve a Tagalog speaker. THE DELTA BETWEEN THE TWO CLIPS IS THE LESSON — and it matters most because RTGS drops tones, so the audio is the only carrier of them.

en-US.why: AMERICAN on purpose: he reads that string with an American ear, so the bridge must approximate THAT reading. 'Neutral / Informative' rather than a performer — the bridge is a reference, not a character.

fil-PH._status: PROVISIONAL — her first language was given by Jordan, not by her. She is the authority on her own language and has not confirmed it yet.
fil-PH.why: A clear reporter's articulation rather than a performer, because the bridge is a REFERENCE. Added from the shared library 2026-10-17 (free) and proven synthesis-capable with a 16,761-byte probe.
fil-PH._open_second_layer: HALF DONE, and this file should say so: the READING TEXT is still spelled for an English eye (RTGS — 'phom ma thiao khrap'). Tagalog is phonetically regular and has no 'ph' or 'kh', so her approximation should be re-spelled in Tagalog orthography. Until that layer exists this clip is an English spelling in a Filipino voice — useful, but not yet truly her bridge.

bridge._no_bridge_for_a_language: If a learner's first language has no entry here, the render must SAY SO and serve the Thai alone. Never hand a learner another language's approximation and call it a bridge — same wrong-answer class as borrowing an English voice to speak Thai.
bridge._verified: 2026-10-17 — both by_lang entries listed live from /v1/voices and synthesised successfully on the `suay` test clip.
bridge._bridge_is_not_a_borrowed_voice: A bridge voice reads an APPROXIMATION in the learner's own language — it is NEVER used to speak Thai script. `no_borrowed_voice` still holds: the Thai side stays native-only, and a missing native voice still means refuse.
